contexts.text: On the Hells of sorceresses. General article.
These are they who there become witches, or sorceresses, some of whom are called Sirens. Fully described.
These sorceresses, or Sirens, are grievously punished. Described. SE 232, described.
Sorceresses and magicians there by phantasies induce others to believe that when in one place they are at the same time in another, and even in many places.
Sirens, who are interior sorceresses...
Falsifications are signified by sorceries in the hand ().
Others who were called sorcerers, etc. were among those who studied natural magic...
Witchcrafts () = falsifications.

Pharaoh called the wise ones and the sorcerers () = an abuse of Divine order... Sorcerers = those who pervert Divine order, thus the laws of order. That sorceries and magic are nothing else, is evident from the sorcerers and magicians in the other life, where they abound. (Continued. See Magic.)

Sorceries, and enchantments, in the Word, = the art of presenting falsities so that they appear like truths, and of presenting truths so that they appear like falsities, which is done especially by means of fallacies. Illustrated. AC 7298.
These phantasies are a species of sorceries, for they too are abuses and inversions of Divine order.

A sorceress thou shalt not cause to live () = those with whom anything of the Church has been conjoined with the falsities of the evil of self love; for sorceries = the falsities of the evil of the love of self conjoined with such things as are of the Church. Explained.
It is this conjunction which, in the internal sense, is signified by sorceries. Illustrated.
That sorcerers = those who conjoin the falsities of the evil of self love with the truths of faith, and thus perish, is evident from the several things here, regarded in the internal sense.
The false doctrinals of their Church are called sorceries, because they destroy the truths of faith.
That those are sorcerers who are learned from themselves, and trust only in themselves to such a degree as to love themselves, and to desire to be worshipped as divinities. Illustrated.

Sorcerers, etc. = those who destroy the truths and goods of the Church by scientifics wrongly applied, thus those who learn and teach from Own intelligence, and by means of falsities from the evils of the loves of self and of the world; and thus who do so from the cupidity for gain and honours.
That Balaam was a sorcerer. Illustrated. AE 140.
I said to the sorcerer, Is this your fane? I then opened his interior sight, and he saw the same things as I. TCR 187.
They who have withdrawn themselves from the snares of the world...
If a meretricious wife be skilled in sorceries...
Nothing but the rods of sorcerers.
On sorceries, etc., their origin. Explained.
On sorceries in the other life.
They who suppose that they can do everything from themselves, are accounted among sorcerers and sorceresses; of such there are genera and species...
Interior sorceries, and grosser sorceries. Explained.
Such constitute what is called sorcery. Explained. [NCBS: Swedenborg used the Swedish word trulldom here, instead of Latin.]
On those who use sorcery or sorceries. [NCBS: Swedenborg used the Swedish word trulldom here, instead of Latin.]
On sorcery. [NCBS: Swedenborg used the Swedish word trulldom here, instead of Latin.]
A sorceress, inspected, was turned into a home of serpents.
On sorceresses.
His sorceries availed nothing against them.
Sorceries = the falsities of evil by which [they acted].
Sons of the sorceress () = falsities from the Word falsified.
